description: NAND-tree evaluation decides who wins a two-player game tree with a continuous-time quantum walk. The player to move wins when some move leaves the opponent in a lost position, so a node's value is the NAND of its children's values, and the leaves are the inputs. The walk graph is the balanced tree with one extra leaf below every `true` input and one extra node `r′` above the root, joined to it with weight `N^(−1/4)` for `N` leaves; its weighted adjacency matrix is the Hamiltonian `H`. `H` has an eigenvalue-0 eigenvector with weight on `r′` exactly when the root is `true`, and a gap around 0 of order `1/√N` seen from `r′` when it is `false`. Phase estimation of `e^(iHτ)` from `r′`, with `τ = π / (fan-out + 1)` and `K` outcomes, `K` the next power of two of `16·√N`, measures outcome `0` with probability at least about `0.35` for a `true` root and at most about `0.05` for a `false` one; the evaluation reports `true` when more than a fifth of the runs see outcome `0`. The inputs sit in `H`, so evolution time plays the part of queries: one run costs `(K − 1)·τ`, against `Θ(N^0.753)` leaf reads for randomized classical evaluation of a binary tree, but the constants put the crossover between about 300 and 1200 leaves. The simulator applies `e^(iHτ)` by its Taylor series, computes the outcome-0 probability exactly and samples the runs from it.
